description: Early control operand forwarding with consumer interlocks: timing-accepted intermediate b207eb2 hardware and complete board measurements, before the subsequent cache-cancel correction.

architecture.execution_unit_parameter: EARLY_CONTROL defaults to 0; the CPU selects LOAD_FORWARDING.
architecture.ordinary_data_path: Completed ordinary loads can forward to data arithmetic, ordinary address computation and store data.
architecture.control_path: Branch, JALR, atomics, and dependent ordinary addresses while data triggers are enabled interlock behind loads and use the early control operands; MEM control forwarding excludes completed load data.
architecture.unchanged_control_contract: Older faults and trigger/trap priority remain precise; standalone execution-unit users default to the previous operand selection unless EARLY_CONTROL is enabled with the matching CPU interlocks.

geometry.checks: Independent integer Delaunay/orientation/hull/manifold predicates; every frame points and triangle ordering matches the accepted baseline.

frozen_uart_metadata.description: Bounded through final 64-point mesh S32DONE; intermediate b207eb2 board candidate, all tests before fetch-cancel correction

software_comparison.interpretation: User application bytes match. Kernel Image/config and initramfs archives differ after clock/DTB/license regeneration; this is an end-to-end comparison, not a strict clock-only Linux experiment.

notes: These CoreMark results are simulated 50-iteration performance and validation seed runs at a nominal 1 MHz timer and 20-cycle AXI model. They are not FPGA scores or physical run medians.
Both seed sets validate CRCs and run for more than 29 simulated seconds. Counter events overlap and must not be added into a CPI decomposition.
CPU retirement counters use EX completion; Linux boot cycle counts describe the entire boot/test sequence rather than the timed CoreMark region.

The b207eb2 bitstream passes timing and board functional/benchmark validation, but is an intermediate result rather than an overall performance winner: bare-metal throughput improves while Linux CoreMark regresses.

Measurements precede the cache-cancel correction. Root cause investigation found that registered cancellation can still admit a same-edge old fallthrough DDR grant; a separate cache-cancel-div16 candidate will preserve these artifacts unchanged.
SQLite workload database, journal and temporary data are in memory; its mixed queries have different costs and do not measure disk I/O.
The complete growing Linux reader log is not hashed. The frozen capture ends after the final 64-point mesh completion and contains all benchmark/application output used here.
